answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with staked identity plus random audits. Each agent locks collateral to mint one key; a scheduler sends surprise challenges, demanding a signed reply within a tight delta window that peers vouch for. Late or duplicated replies slash the bond and revoke the key. Since probes arrive like a gale, an attacker cannot keep idle accounts cheaply: each fake identity needs its own deposit, tracked in a juniper voucher tree of human-backed leaves. Cloning that tree costs more than any honest agent earns, so the farm bleeds out before it gains trust.
